title: Continuous batch smoothing and KV thrift budgeting for mixed-priority inference
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: We need a runtime-level policy that reduces OOM and eviction storms by smoothing admission into continuous batching and introducing a small, reclaimable KV 'thrift' budget that dynamically shifts between weights/KV/activations. This ticket prototypes the algorithm, implements a conservative scheduler in the canary runtime, and wires telemetry+dashboards to validate headroom behavior under mixed-priority workloads (low-latency interactive vs. throughput batch).
acceptance_criteria: Conservative batch-smoothing admission implemented in the runtime and enabled behind a feature flag in canary region
KV thrift pool implemented: configurable size (bytes or percent), LRU lease semantics, and preemption priority tiers
End-to-end tests that simulate mixed-priority traffic and show reduced KV eviction spikes compared to baseline
Telemetry dashboard with: KV evictions/sec, thrift pool utilization, per-tenant headroom margin, tail token-latency P99 before/after
Rollout playbook documented and rollback path validated
Performance regression within SLA: <5% median latency increase and tail latency deterioration within agreed safety band for interactive workloads
tasks: Design and doc algorithm for batch smoothing + thrift budgeting (spec link)
Implement admission controller hook that smooths the batch size growth over 200ms window
Add thrift pool allocator in GPU memory ledger with lease metadata and tiered preemption
Integrate eviction metrics into runtime telemetry and extend console dashboard
Create workload simulator that mixes 90/10 interactive/batch profiles and run before/after experiments
Canary deploy in eu-west-1 to 5 dedicated nodes, collect 72h of data
Review and safety sign-off with SRE and Product, plan gradual rollout
technical_notes: Rationale: continuous batching currently admits bursts that cause KV eviction cascades; smoothing reduces instantaneous KV pressure and amortizes activation allocations

Thrift budget: small, opportunistic allocation (default 4% of GPU memory) that is given to lower-priority requests and reclaimed immediately on preemption. Implemented as soft-backed 'lease' entries in KV ledger
Lease semantics: leases have decay-weights and renewal costs; eviction will remove thrift entries first, then low-priority canonical KV slots, then activations in older requests
Admission smoothing window tuned by 95th-percentile request arrival variance; initial conservative value = 200ms, adjustable via runtime flag
Memory accounting: introduce 'elastic' and 'pinned' tags for allocations. Weights remain pinned; KV entries can be elastic with a min-reservation
Fallback: when thrift pool exhausted and pressure remains, route new requests to slower model variant (quantized) or enqueue with backpressure depending on policy
Compatibility: must respect Dedicated tenant isolation — thrift pool exists per-GPU and is controlled by tenant config when Dedicated is enabled
